explanation: The FAA requests a minimum of 2,000 feet above the surface over charted national parks, wildlife refuges and similar noise-sensitive areas.

stem: Unless each occupant wears an approved parachute, no pilot carrying a passenger may intentionally exceed a bank of
options: 60 degrees, or a nose-up or nose-down attitude of 30 degrees
90 degrees, or a nose-up or nose-down attitude of 45 degrees
45 degrees, or a nose-up or nose-down attitude of 20 degrees
explanation: 14 CFR 91.307(c) sets the limits at 60 degrees of bank or 30 degrees of pitch relative to the horizon, except for certificate training given by a flight instructor.

stem: In the Northern Hemisphere, turning from a heading of north, the magnetic compass will initially
options: lead the turn by a large amount
show a turn in the opposite direction
show the correct heading at all times
explanation: Northerly turning error (from magnetic dip) makes the compass lag in turns from a north heading, first swinging the opposite way, and lead in turns from a south heading.

stem: Which is a sign that fatigue is affecting a pilot's performance?
options: Scanning the instruments faster than normal and more widely
Missing radio calls and making small, careless errors
Feeling more alert and confident than at the start of the day
explanation: Fatigue shows up as slower reactions, narrowed attention, missed calls and careless mistakes. The only cure is rest.

stem: At night in Class G airspace below 1,200 feet AGL, an airplane may fly with 1 mile visibility clear of clouds only when
options: it is flying with a filed and activated VFR flight plan
it is in an airport traffic pattern within half a mile of the runway
it is more than 10 miles from the nearest airport with a control tower
explanation: 14 CFR 91.155(b)(2) allows 1 statute mile and clear of clouds at night in Class G below 1,200 feet AGL only in a traffic pattern within half a mile of the runway. Otherwise 3 miles and 500/1,000/2,000 apply.

stem: Which cloud type indicates very unstable air and the most hazardous flying conditions?
options: Cumulonimbus
Nimbostratus
Altostratus
explanation: Cumulonimbus are thunderstorm clouds with turbulence, icing, hail, lightning and wind shear. Nimbostratus and altostratus are layered clouds in more stable air.

stem: What does a convective outlook describe?
options: The present location of thunderstorms detected by weather radar
The potential for severe and general thunderstorms over the coming days
Turbulence and icing forecast in the lower layers of the atmosphere for the next 12 hours
explanation: The Storm Prediction Center's convective outlook forecasts where general and severe thunderstorms may develop over the next days, useful for planning. Radar shows storms that exist now.

stem: Loading an airplane so the CG is aft of its limit makes it
options: less stable and harder to recover from a stall or spin
nose heavy, so it needs more back pressure to flare
more stable and easier to recover from a stall or spin
explanation: An aft CG shortens the tail's lever arm for recovery, so the airplane is less stable in pitch and stall or spin recovery may be difficult or impossible.

stem: Which correction turns a magnetic heading into a compass heading?
options: Deviation, read from the airplane's compass correction card
Wind correction angle, worked out on the E6B flight computer before departure
Variation, read from the isogonic lines on the chart
explanation: True course, plus wind correction, gives true heading; variation gives magnetic heading; the airplane's own deviation card gives compass heading.

stem: How long is a passed FAA knowledge test result valid for taking the private pilot practical test?
options: 12 calendar months
24 calendar months
36 calendar months
explanation: 14 CFR 61.39 requires the knowledge test to have been passed within the preceding 24 calendar months before the practical test.

stem: Why is a propeller blade twisted along its length?
options: To reduce noise at the highest power settings
To make the blade tips turn more slowly than the blade roots at the hub
To keep a more even angle of attack from hub to tip
explanation: The tip moves much faster than the hub, so the blade angle decreases toward the tip to give a fairly even angle of attack and thrust along the blade.
